newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate steady, seen easing-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate steady, seen easing-dealers.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate was steady around 25.00 percent in late trade on Friday against 25.00-26.00 percent early on extremely tight liquidity, dealers said.
But the interbank rate showed signs of easing as banks were willing to lend funds in the market late in the afternoon after the bi-monthly reserve requirement passed, dealers said.
"The interbank rate was dealt as high as 28 and 30 percent in the morning. But the rate eased to around 25 percent in the late afternoon," one dealer at a U.S. bank said.
Dealers attributed the strong demand for funds today to the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement which came due today and seasonal high spending for Lunar New Year.
All commercial banks have to meet the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
Heavy purchases of the dollar over the past few weeks also tightened the money supply, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 25.990/26.040 to the dollar in dull trade compared with 26.000/26.010 early, dealers said.
"The volume was very light today. Most players in Singapore and Hong Kong were on holiday," said one dealer at a European bank.
Dealers said the dollar's strength against major currencies prompted some continued buying of the U.S. unit in the market today.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.92 baht per dollar, the lowest level in more than five years. The mid-rate was at 25.90 on Thursday.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 19.00/20.00 satangs per dollar late against 18.00/19.00 in the morning, dealers said.-- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
